}}'''Jared Dane McCain''' (born February 20, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and ranked among the top players in the 2023 class. McCain played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] before being selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] as the 16th overall pick in the first round of the [[2024 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
McCain attended [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High School]] in [[Corona, California]], graduating in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/03/04/alexander-centennials-jared-mccain-is-a-social-media-star|title=Alexander: Centennial's Jared McCain is a social media star|first=Jim|last=Alexander|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=May 4, 2022|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref> As a junior, he was named the 2021–22 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] for boys basketball in [[California]] after averaging 16.9 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game. During this time, McCain appeared in three seasons of the [[YouTube]] [[Television documentary|docuseries]] ''Believe'', directed and filmed by Nick Ramos.<ref>{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Luca |date=November 13, 2022 |title=Centennial hoop star Jared McCain building a potential fortune |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/story/2022-11-13/centennial-basketball-star-jared-mccain-is-building-potential-fortune |access-date=April 18, 2023 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> In his senior year, he was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Johnson |first=Eric-Paul |date=January 25, 2023 |title=Centennial boys basketball star Jared McCain chosen for McDonald's All-American Game |url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2023/01/25/centennial-boys-basketball-star-jared-mccain-chosen-for-mcdonalds-all-american-game |access-date=April 30, 2023 |work=[[The Press-Enterprise]]}}</ref> McCain repeated as the 2022–23 Gatorade Player of the Year for boys basketball in California after averaging 17.7 points, 7.1 rebounds, 4.0 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Johnson |first=Eric-Paul |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Centennial's Jared McCain again chosen Gatorade's California boys basketball player of the year |url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2023/03/16/centennials-jared-mccain-again-chosen-gatorades-california-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |access-date=May 3, 2023 |work=[[The Press-Enterprise]]}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
McCain was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and ranked among the top players in the 2023 class according to major recruiting services.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lawson |first=Theo |date=March 18, 2022 |title=Class of 2023 five-star prospect Jared McCain commits to Duke over Gonzaga, others |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/mar/18/class-of-2023-five-star-prospect-jared-mccain-comm/ |access-date=April 3, 2023 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35046354/duke-commit-jared-mccain-signs-excel-sports|title=Duke commit Jared McCain signs with Excel Sports|first=Myron|last=Medcalf|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 17, 2022|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref> He verbally committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] on March 18, 2022, and signed his [[National Letter of Intent|national letter of intent]] on November 9. McCain chose Duke over offers from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |name-list-style=and |date=March 18, 2022 |title=Duke Blue Devils get verbal commitment from five-star junior guard Jared McCain in 2023 class |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33540308 |access-date=April 3, 2023 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |authorlink2=Paul Biancardi}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10030239-5-star-sg-jared-mccain-commits-to-duke-over-gonzaga-houston-more|title=5-Star SG Jared McCain Commits to Duke over Gonzaga, Houston, More|first=Doric|last=Sam|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=March 18, 2022|access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
McCain enrolled at [[Duke University]] in June 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/article/dukes-freshman-class-together-at-k-academy-211031411/|title=LOOK: Duke's freshman class together at K Academy|first=Adam|last=Rowe|website=[[247Sports]]|date=June 2, 2023|access-date=July 20, 2023}}</ref> He made his [[college basketball]] debut on November 6, 2023, scoring 8 points in 15 minutes in a 92–54 win over [[2023–24 Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball team|Dartmouth]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dartmouth 54-92 Duke (Nov 6, 2023) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401576147 |access-date=November 15, 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>  On January 27, 2024, McCain scored 21 points and grabbed 5 rebounds during a 72–71 victory against [[2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401604148|title=Tyrese Proctor's late free throws help No.12 Duke hold off Clemson 72-71|date=January 27, 2024|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref> He was named the [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) Rookie of the Week on January 29.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2024/1/29/athlete-awards-uncs-davis-dukes-mccain-earn-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|title=UNC's Davis, Duke's McCain Earn ACC Men's Basketball Weekly Honors|date=January 29, 2024|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref> McCain recorded a career-high 35 points on February 17, tying the Duke freshman record previously held by [[Zion Williamson]], in a 76–67 win against [[2023–24 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401604194|title=Duke's McCain sets freshman 3-point mark, ties frosh scoring record in 76-67 win over Florida State|date=February 17, 2024|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=March 23, 2024}}</ref> For this performance, he received ACC Rookie of the Week honors again on February 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2024/2/19/pitts-hinson-dukes-mccain-earn-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|title=Pitt's Hinson, Duke's McCain Earn ACC Men's Basketball Weekly Honors|date=February 19, 2024|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref> On March 24, he contributed 30 points and 5 rebounds in a 93–55 victory over [[2023–24 James Madison Dukes men's basketball team|James Madison]].<ref>{{cite web |date=March 25, 2024 |title=Jared McCain makes 8 3s, scores 30 points as Duke ends James Madison's March Madness run |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401638627 |access-date=March 28, 2024 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> In the [[Elite Eight]] round of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2024 NCAA tournament]] on March 31, McCain scored 32 points in a 76–64 loss to [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]]. He concluded his freshman [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|season]] averaging 14.3 points and 5.0 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2024/04/duke-mens-basketball-jared-mccain-player-review-2023-24-tiktok-bilas-nba|title=Duke men's basketball 2023–24 player review: Jared McCain|last=Tan|first=Jun|date=April 14, 2024|website=[[Duke Chronicle]]|access-date=March 24, 2025}}</ref>

After the conclusion of the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]], McCain declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] on April 12, 2024, forgoing his remaining [[National Collegiate Athletic Association#Player eligibility|college eligibility]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salerno |first=Cameron |date=April 12, 2024 |title=2024 NBA Draft: Duke's Jared McCain to go pro after earning ACC All-Rookie Team honors |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2024-nba-draft-dukes-jared-mccain-to-go-pro-after-earning-acc-all-rookie-team-honors/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> He later received an invitation to the draft [[2024 NBA draft#Invited attendees|green room]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salerno |first=Cameron |date=June 19, 2024 |title=2024 NBA Draft: UConn's Donovan Clingan, French prospects among 24 players to accept green room invites |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2024-nba-draft-uconns-donovan-clingan-french-prospects-among-24-players-to-accept-green-room-invites/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2024–2026)===
McCain was selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] as the 16th overall pick in the first round of the [[2024 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2024 |title=Jared McCain Selected by 76ers in First Round of 2024 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-select-jared-mccain-first-round-2024-nba-draft |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=Sixers Basketball}}</ref> He signed a four-year contract with the team on July 4, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 4, 2024 |title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN 2024 FIRST-ROUND DRAFT PICK JARED MCCAIN |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-2024-first-round-draft-pick-jared-mccain |access-date=July 5, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

McCain made his [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) debut on October 23, 2024, in a 124–109 loss to the [[2024–25 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks at Philadelphia 76ers Box Score, October 23, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410230PHI.html|website=BasketballRef|access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> On November 13, he recorded a career-high 34 points and 10 assists in a 114–106 loss to the [[2024–25 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-news-how-jared-mccain-overtaken-rookie-of-year-odds|title=How 76ers' Jared McCain has overtaken Rookie of the Year odds|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pursiainen|first=Kris|date=November 14, 2024|access-date=November 22, 2024}}</ref> He was named the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Rookie of the Month]] for October and November after leading all NBA rookies with 16.0 points per game over 18 appearances, becoming the first 76ers player to receive the honor since [[Ben Simmons]] in March 2018.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 3, 2024 |title=Monthly NBA awards: Jayson Tatum, Victor Wembanyama win honors for Oct. and Nov. |url=https://www.nba.com/news/monthly-nba-awards-october-november-2024 |access-date=November 16, 2024 |website=[[NBA]]}}</ref> On December 14, it was announced that McCain had suffered a [[meniscus tear]] in his left knee, sidelining him indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|title=Sixers rookie Jared McCain out indefinitely with lateral meniscus tear in left knee |url=https://www.nba.com/news/sixers-jared-mccain-lateral-meniscus-tear-left-knee |date=December 14, 2024|access-date=December 15, 2024 |publisher=[[Associated Press]]|via=[[NBA.com]]|language=en}}</ref> On January 10, 2025, it was officially reported that he would miss the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Andrew |title=76ers' Jared McCain Out for Rest of Season After Meniscus Surgery on Knee Injury |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10150314-76ers-jared-mccain-out-for-rest-of-season-after-meniscus-surgery-on-knee-injury |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

On October 1, 2025, the 76ers announced that McCain had undergone [[surgery]] to repair a tear in the [[Ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|ulnar collateral ligament]] (UCL) of his right thumb. As a result, he was expected to miss at least one month of play.<ref>{{cite web | last=Harris | first=Declan | title=Sixers Confirm Jared McCain Surgery, Provide Initial Timeline | website=Philadelphia 76ers On SI | date=2025-10-01 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/onsi/news/sixers-confirm-jared-mccain-surgery-provide-initial-timeline-01k6fft0d2k7 | access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref> McCain made 37 appearances (including one start) for Philadelphia during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 6.6 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jared McCain 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683778/jared-mccain|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2026–present)===
On February 4, 2026, McCain was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for a 2026 first-round pick and three second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-mccain-260204|title=Thunder Acquires Jared McCain|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2026}}</ref> On February 7, McCain made his Thunder debut, putting up five points in a 112–106 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/oklahoma-city-thunder/thunder-news-mark-daigneault-gives-instant-reaction-jared-mccain-debut|title=Thunder’s Mark Daigneault gives instant reaction to Jared McCain’s debut|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pavon|first=Josue|date=February 7, 2026|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2026/02/07/rockets-vs-thunder-score-okc-injury-report-kevin-durant-tari-eason-stats/88566742007/|title=Tari Eason fuels Rockets past Thunder as OKC suffers second straight loss|website=The Oklahoman|last=Davis|first=Jordan|date=February 7, 2026|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref> On May 22, McCain had a playoff career-high 24 points in a 123–108 victory over the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in game 3 of the [[NBA conference finals|2026 Western Conference Finals]].<ref>{{citeweb|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7301939/2026/05/22/thunder-spurs-game-3-result-western-conference-finals-nba/|title=Jared McCain erupts as Thunder weather Spurs’ fast start, seize 2–1 series lead|last1=Lorenzi|first1=Joel|last2=Weiss|first2=Jared|last3=Hollinger|first3=John|last4=Harkins|first4=Bob|publisher=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 22, 2026|accessdate=May 23, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
McCain represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|2022 FIBA U18 Americas Championship]] held in [[Tijuana|Tijuana, Mexico]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 12, 2022 |title=USA Wins Gold at 2022 FIBA MU18 Americas Championship |url=https://www.usab.com/news/2022/06/mu18-usa-bra-recap |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref> He played in all six games during the tournament and contributed to the team’s undefeated 6–0 record, which earned them the gold medal. Throughout the competition, he averaged 11.2 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game, while shooting 41.5 percent from the field.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jared McCain - USA - Player profile - FIBA U18 Americas Championship |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/256-fiba-u18-americup/208444/players/318723-jared-mccain |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=[[FIBA|FIBA Basketball]]}}</ref>

== Media and endorsements ==
McCain gained recognition on [[social media]] platforms, particularly [[TikTok]] and [[YouTube]], by posting basketball-related content, personal vlogs, and participating in trending dance challenges. Notably, in January 2024, McCain posted a video to the song [[2 Days into College|''2 Days into College'']] by [[Aimee Carty]], which proceeded to go viral. His activity on these platforms throughout his years at [[Duke University]] and joining the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] contributed to his growth as an [[influencer]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marks |first=Brendan |date=October 17, 2024 |title=Jared McCain is Duke basketball’s latest talent, but he’s more famous for dancing on TikTok |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4966809/2023/10/17/jared-mccain-duke-basketball-tiktok-dance/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

McCain is of [[Multiracial people|mixed racial]] heritage. His mother, Jina, is an [[Americans|American]] with both [[White Americans|White]] and [[Filipinos|Filipino]] ancestry. His father, Lance, is [[African Americans|African American]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Ashmit |date=November 26, 2024 |title=Is Jared McCain From the Philippines? About 76ers Star’s Ethnicity, Nationality, Family Roots, and Upbringing |url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nba-active-basketball-news-what-is-jared-mccain-s-ethnicity-all-about-philadelphia-76ers-star-s-nationality-family-roots-and-upbringing/#:~:text=%5BI'm%5D%20Probably%20like,mother,%20Jina,%20is%20white. |access-date=November 28, 2024 |website=EssentiallySports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Agcaoili |first=Lance |date=November 28, 2024 |title=Jared McCain, NBA rising star, says he’s partly Filipino |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/596244/jared-mccain-nba-rising-star-says-hes-partly-filipino |access-date=December 5, 2024 |website=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer|INQUIRER.net]]}}</ref>

McCain has one sibling, an older brother named Jayce. Jayce played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cal State San Marcos Cougars]] and, as of October 2025, is serving as the Player Development Specialist for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jayce McCain - Player Development Specialist - Staff Directory |url=https://goduke.com/staff-directory/jayce-mccain/1420 |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=[[Duke Blue Devils]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jayce McCain |url=https://liberalstudies.duke.edu/jayce-mccain/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=Duke Graduate Liberal Studies}}</ref>
